## Proposed change
The existing stream component sends a blank stream of audio along with its video stream. This PR muxes the audio stream into the output HLS stream if the codec is supported. If not, no audio stream is sent along with the video, saving bandwidth.
Note that PCM codecs such as G.711 are not supported as they are not supported in mp4 containers.

Just tested this PR with a Reolink RLC-420 5MP stream. Works perfectly. Thanks for this! :+1: 

Oh also, fixes #29807

@hunterjm I looked more into getting G.711 (pcm_mulaw) to work. Unfortunately, without transcoding it's not doable in HLS since pcm_mulaw does not mux into mp4 or mpegts using ffmpeg. One workaround would be to relax the container compliance check here: https://github.com/PyAV-Org/PyAV/blob/main/av/container/output.pyx#L75 , but even if you get it into the containers, the players might not play it.
For recording, it is doable, but not in mp4. Matroska should support pcm_mulaw, but I think the codec tag for pcm_mulaw is missing in the matroska ffmpeg implementation. Anyway, quicktime mov works.
However, we have the problem of lookback - the lookback segments come from the HLS queue, so they won't have any audio.
I've worked up a solution to this by splitting out the audio and video streams into separate containers in each Segment. This makes it easier to treat the audio stream diferently when pcm_mulaw is detected. While this won't get you audio over HLS, it should get you audio in recorder as well as in the lookback. I think that is probably pretty useful when recording an event.
Let me know if you want me to push those changes.
Edit:
Reasons not to push the change - Added complexity just for supporting G.711 in Recorder. Many devices which can use G.711 don't even have internal mics. Mov is not as standardized as mp4. There is additional overhead when serving separate audio and video streams in HLS.

One more thing - some codec variations like Hikvision H264+/H265+ use techniques which reduce the number of keyframes, resulting in segments that are quite long and sometimes uneven. While they seem to work in my testing, some issues this may introduce include players not starting as close to the live edge as desired and lookback/recorder durations being longer than requested. The bandwidth savings are great though.

Regarding G.711 - When I was looking at implementing audio initially my camera didn't support AAC. Audio transcoding doesn't have anywhere near the same overhead as video transcoding, so I was looking to transcode it to a supported format but got stuck with time sync issues in the output. I think it'd be great to include as an option for the `stream` component to transcode audio for selected streams in the future (similar to the preload stream option), but that doesn't need to be in this PR.

I'm checking this PR out locally now to start testing. I noticed you added a few more commits. Is this in it's final state or are you still tinkering with things?
